IC1: Administration of the licensed MF59-containing vaccines [OR], e.g. Fluad [OR]™ or Addigrip™ or virosome-based influenza vaccines such as Inflexal V [OR]™, InfectoVac Flu [OR]™ or Invivac™ during the 2006-2007 influenza season.
IC2: Administration of licensed vaccines within 2 weeks (for inactivated vaccines [OR]) or 4 weeks (for live vaccines) prior to enrolment in this study.
IC3: Planned administration of a vaccine not [OR] foreseen by the study protocol up to 30 days after the second [AND] vaccination [AND] with H5N1 vaccine.
IC4: Chronic administration (defined as more than 14 days) of immunosuppressants or other immune-modifying drugs within six months prior to the first administration of the study vaccine.
IC5: Any confirmed [OR] or suspected immunosuppressive [OR] or immunodeficient condition, based on medical history and physical examination (no laboratory testing required).
IC6: History of chronic alcohol consumption [OR] and/or drug abuse.
IC8: History of allergic [OR] disease or reactions likely to be exacerbated by any component of the vaccine (including egg and thiomersal allergy).
IC9: Acute clinically significant pulmonary [OR], cardiovascular [OR], hepatic [OR] or renal functional abnormality, as determined by physical examination or laboratory screening tests.
IC10: Acute disease at the time of enrolment.
IC11: Serious chronic disease including any medically significant chronic [OR] pulmonary [OR], cardiovascular, renal, neurological, psychiatric or metabolic disorder, as determined by medical history and physical examination.
IC12: Administration of immunoglobulins [OR] and/or any blood products within the three months preceding the first vaccination [OR] or during the study.
IC13: Use of any investigational [OR] or non-registered product [AND] (drug [OR] or vaccine) [NOT] other than the study vaccine(s) within 30 days prior to the first vaccination, or planned use during the study period.
IC14: Any condition which [AND], in the opinion of the investigator, prevents the subject from participation in the study.
